transcript: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Over the past year our team has built a tool that helps people improve the way they speak. It listens to a recording, compares it with a clear example of the same message, and shows exactly where the delivery changed. For instance, you might speak too quickly during a key point, or pause for too long before an answer. The tool marks those moments on a timeline, explains what it measured, and suggests one simple change. We tested it with students, teachers, and engineers, and most of them improved within a single week. Today I will show you how it works, step by step. Please feel free to ask questions at any time.

flaws.explanation: 24.1–26.0 s: a pause of 1.90 s inside a phrase after “quickly” and before “during”, 1.66 s longer than the baseline mean pause of 0.24 s (29.94 standard deviations above it). Flagged because the pause was more than 2.0 standard deviations longer than the baseline mean, which is a longer break than in the baseline delivery.
flaws.recommendation: Keep these words connected: aim for a pause close to 0.24 s, as in the baseline delivery.
warnings: The pause type (within a phrase or between sentences) is inferred from the transcript's punctuation.

flaws.explanation: 38.2–51.1 s: speech rate averaged 83.5 words/min, 40.9% below the baseline mean of 141.2 words/min (4.85 standard deviations below it), covering “change.” to “week.”. Flagged because the rate was more than 2.0 standard deviations below the baseline mean over at least 0.5 s, which indicates slower delivery compared with the baseline.
flaws.recommendation: Bring the pace up in this stretch towards the baseline pace of about 141.2 words/min and link phrases together without long gaps.
warnings: Speech rate is detected over rolling windows and the finding is then narrowed to the words that were faster or slower, so its start and end can still be off by a word or two. Its standard-deviation figure compares this short stretch with the spread of the baseline's windows, scaled for the stretch having fewer words to average over.

overall_summary: 2 delivery deviations from the baseline were detected in 59.7 s of analysed speech (too slow: 1, excessive pause: 1). Deviation score: 78.0 out of 100 across speech rate, pauses and energy (100 means no deviation was detected). Not evaluated: pitch. These results compare delivery with the baseline recording; they are not a measure of speech quality or content. Detection thresholds and score weights are initial values that have not yet been calibrated on recorded data.

notes.message: Detection thresholds and score weights are initial values that have not been calibrated on recorded data; treat findings and scores as indicative.

Pitch was not evaluated and is not part of the score: flat_pitch: baseline has no statistic of F0 variation within a window (BaselineStats holds only the pooled global F0 std); detection not implemented.
